verbatim_locators.note: COVERAGE: whole article read, Table 1 read, both figures (schematics) inspected as images. A narrative mini-review: no methods or results sections, no limitations section; the reference list (66) was screened for integrity, not read, so every statement is a restatement of a cited source.

entries.proposition: DESIGN: a mini-review whose two writers state they researched the literature; no search strategy, no appraisal; every number is a restatement.
entries.snippet: L.H. and S.M. researched literature and wrote the manuscript.

entries.proposition: The glucose thresholds used are diabetes-clinic definitions: 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L) or lower with symptoms, level 2 below 54 mg/dL; they are adult standards and say nothing about neonatal or genetic-metabolic ranges.
entries.snippet: In numerical terms, a value of 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L) or lower with associated symptoms is usually considered a hypoglycemic condition.

entries.proposition: COUNTER-REGULATION: epinephrine is one of the hormones whose release falls after recent antecedent hypoglycaemia; the review states that absence of symptoms reflects attenuation of the sympathoadrenal response.
entries.snippet: The absence of symptoms of hypoglycemia reflects the attenuation of the sympathoadrenal response

entries.proposition: The epinephrine statement is that after recent antecedent hypoglycaemia plasma epinephrine rises less; no value, no cohort and no time course are given in the review.
entries.snippet: After recent antecedent hypoglycemia, epinephrine levels are significantly reduced (Figure 2)

entries.proposition: GLYCOGEN: the review states brain cells cannot store glucose as glycogen; astrocytes do hold glycogen, and another review in this corpus (a metabolic-batch reading of brain glycogen) treats it as a buffer; the sentence is a simplification or an error.
entries.snippet: It is not possible for cells in the brain to synthesize glucose or to store it as glycogen.

entries.proposition: The role of the other hormones is partly open: growth hormone matters in prolonged hypoglycaemia, and the review says the exact role of cortisol remains unclear.
entries.snippet: However, the exact role of cortisol in hypoglycemia counterregulation remains unclear.

entries.proposition: A central mechanism offered is raised GABA inhibitory tone in the ventromedial hypothalamus after recurrent hypoglycaemia, hedged with "could be important".
entries.snippet: Recurrent hypoglycemia results in increased VMH GABA inhibitory tone which could be important in the development of a hypoglycemia unawareness syndrome

entries.proposition: Sleep: awakening with an epinephrine rise during nocturnal clamp hypoglycaemia was impaired in type 1 diabetes against controls; a three-clamp study found the response preserved after sleep loss and attenuated after regular sleep, which the review calls neurometabolic memory.
entries.snippet: Awakening from sleep with an accompanying increase in epinephrine levels was impaired in patients with T1D compared to healthy controls

entries.proposition: The review suggests sleep loss after repeated hypoglycaemia might prevent unawareness, a speculation from one study that the authors say needs further investigation.
entries.snippet: sleep loss after repeated hypoglycemia could prevent hypoglycemia unawareness

entries.proposition: POPULATION: children appear only for nocturnal hypoglycaemia after exercise; there is no neonatal, genetic or encephalopathy content.
entries.snippet: Especially in children and adolescents, nocturnal hypoglycemia can occur after delayed effects of exercise and alterations in sleep physiology.

entries.proposition: Figure 2 is a schematic: a timeline of first, second and third hypoglycaemia over a falling wedge labelled growth hormone, epinephrine, glucagon; no axis, quantity or source data.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 2: arrow with ticks 1st, 2nd and 3rd hypoglycemia over a downward-sloping band labelled Hypoglycemia counterregulation: Growth Hormone, Epinephrine, Glucagon.
